parameters.content:
## Try it in 3 steps

**1.** Drop one or more call recordings into the repo's `./audio/` folder (any common format - mp3, wav, m4a, ogg...).

**2.** Open the *ingestion* path below and click **Execute workflow**. Each file runs through the full GPU pipeline (expect a few minutes per call on first run while models warm up).

**3.** Open the **Chat** panel on the *chat* path and ask things like:
- "what calls do we have?"
- "show me the dashboard"
- "did any client push back on price?"
- "give me the report for call <call_id>"

options.systemMessage:
You are a call-analysis assistant for processed sales calls.

Tools available (pick the right one):
1. recent_calls — most recent calls, ordered newest first. Use for "the latest", "today's", "the last N calls", "this week's calls".
2. search_calls — semantic content search. Use for questions about WHAT was said (objections, themes, similar calls).
3. get_call_report — direct lookup by exact call_id. Use only when the user gives a call_id or another tool returned one.
4. get_dashboard — headline metrics + an inline image of the dashboard. Use when the user asks for a DASHBOARD, METRICS, AT-A-GLANCE summary, performance report, or visual overview. Modes:
   - name="overview" for cross-call counters
   - name="closer" with closer_name=<name> for one-closer breakdown

Decision tree:
- "how are calls going?" / "this week's stats" / "overall metrics" → get_dashboard(name="overview").
- "how is <name> performing?" / "<name>'s dashboard" / "<name>'s last calls" → get_dashboard(name="closer", closer_name="<name>").
- "latest call" / "most recent" → recent_calls.
- Content question → search_calls.
- Specific call_id → get_call_report.

How to present a dashboard response (CRITICAL):
When get_dashboard returns an `image_url` field, your reply MUST embed that image inline using EXACTLY this Markdown syntax:
    ![Dashboard](IMAGE_URL_HERE)
Replace IMAGE_URL_HERE with the exact value of image_url from the tool response — do not modify it. Put the image first, then summarise the key_metrics in 2–4 short bullets, then on its own line add [Open dashboard full size](IMAGE_URL_HERE) with the same image_url, so the user can always click through even if the inline image does not render.

How to deliver call reports (CRITICAL):
Whenever a tool response contains pdf_url and/or html_url that are not null, you MUST end your reply with a 'Report:' line containing them as Markdown links, e.g.
    Report: [PDF](PDF_URL_HERE) · [HTML](HTML_URL_HERE)
using the exact URL values from the tool response. This chat cannot attach files — these links ARE the delivery, so never omit them. If both are null, say the report has not been rendered yet and that opening the link will generate it.

Never invent links or numbers — only use URLs and values that appear verbatim in tool responses, and quote numbers exactly as returned.

Rules:
- Do not invent facts. Quote tool output directly.
- If a tool returns nothing, say so plainly.
- For non-dashboard tools, prefer concise bullets when listing multiple calls.
- Numbers come straight from call_reports — quote them as-is.

parameters.toolDescription: Fetch the executive report for ONE specific call by exact call_id. Renders the PDF/HTML on first request (cached afterwards) and returns pdf_url, html_url, summary, received_at. ALWAYS include the returned pdf_url/html_url as Markdown links in your reply. DO NOT use this for "latest" or "most recent" — use recent_calls instead.
parameters.url: =http://rag-api:8000/report/{{ $fromAI('call_id', 'The exact call_id to fetch the report for, e.g. 68ef36aece392675', 'string') }}

parameters.content:
## Ingestion path (audio → analytics, one POST)

**Read/Write Files**: reads audio from `/home/node/.n8n-files/audio/*` — the repo's `./audio/` folder. Any common container/codec works: the API normalises everything to 16 kHz mono WAV with ffmpeg, so the input extension doesn't matter downstream.

**Analyze call**: POSTs the audio to call-analysis-api `/scorecard?persist=true&index_utterances=true`. One request runs the full GPU pipeline:

ASR (faster-whisper) → speaker diarization (pyannote) → LLM speaker→role relabel → text sentiment (RoBERTa) → speech emotion (emotion2vec+) → prosody (openSMILE) → PII redaction (Presidio) → entities (GLiNER) → LLM KPIs + coaching rubric (Ollama)

…then persists the call + utterances + events + pgvector embeddings to Postgres in ONE transaction. There is no separate save-to-DB node (`persist=true` does the write), and no PDF is rendered here — reports render lazily on first request via rag-api `/report/{call_id}`.

## Chat path (RAG agent over the processed calls)

**AI Agent** (Ollama + window memory) picks ONE tool per the system-prompt decision tree:

**search_calls** → rag-api `/search`: semantic search. Embeds the query (Ollama Qwen3-Embedding + Matryoshka 2560→1024 truncation) and runs a pgvector cosine match over `calls.summary_embedding`. Use for content / themes / objections ("what was said").

**get_dashboard** → rag-api `/dashboard`: builds the KPI view-model from `calls` and returns an `image_url` to a freshly-rendered dashboard PNG (render-api HTML + Gotenberg screenshot). The agent embeds the image inline in its reply.

**recent_calls** → Postgres `SELECT … ORDER BY received_at DESC`: plain query for latest / today / last-N. No embedding needed.

**get_call_report** → Postgres lookup by exact call_id: returns the summary + report URLs (rag-api `/report/{call_id}` renders the PDF on first request and caches it).

parameters.toolDescription: Semantic search over processed sales calls. Use when the user asks about call CONTENT (objections, sentiment, what was said, themes). Returns up to top_k similar calls with summary, KPIs, and pdf_url. For looking up a SPECIFIC call_id, use get_call_report instead.

Returns the most recent N processed sales calls ordered newest first. Use for any time-based query ("latest call", "most recent", "today", "the last 3 calls"). The first row is the most recent call; its pdf_url is the latest report. Default top_k=5.
parameters.query:
SELECT call_id, received_at, file_name, duration_sec,
       closer_talk_ratio, objection_count, buying_signal_count,
       next_step_secured, rapport_quality, predicted_outcome,
       summary, pdf_url, html_url
FROM calls
ORDER BY received_at DESC
LIMIT GREATEST(1, LEAST(50, {{ $fromAI('top_k', 'How many recent calls to return (1-50). Default 5.', 'number', 5) }}));

parameters.toolDescription:
Return headline KPI metrics and an `image_url` pointing at a freshly-rendered dashboard PNG. Use for high-level performance views. Modes:
  - name="overview": cross-call counters (total calls, calls in last 7 days, avg coaching score, % with next step). Use when the user asks for general/overall/recent stats.
  - name="closer" with closer_name=<name>: per-closer breakdown (calls handled, avg score, win rate %). Use when the user names a specific closer. closer_name is optional; omit it to show all closers combined. Pass date_range to control the time window (today/yesterday/7d/30d/mtd/last_month/all; default 7d, use 'all' for all-time).

parameters.name: closer_name
parameters.value: ={{ $fromAI('closer_name', 'Name of the closer when name=closer. Leave blank for all-closer aggregate.', 'string', '') }}

parameters.name: date_range
parameters.value: ={{ $fromAI('date_range', 'Time window preset: today, yesterday, 7d, 30d, mtd, last_month, or all. Use 7d when the user does not specify; all when they say all time / overall / ever.', 'string', '7d') }}
